title: capacity-fidelity-controller-and-soft-surge-fallback
author: Aisha N. Patel
release_notes: Add Capacity Fidelity Controller: honors throughput fidelity targets per-pool, introduces soft-surge fallback path and new per-pool fidelity metric exposed to Console/telemetry.
description:
Problem and motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally violate per-tenant throughput guarantees during low headroom periods because the existing allocator prioritizes slot occupancy over observed fidelity (observed throughput vs promised throughput). This causes customer visible throughput regressions and noisy incident exercises. This PR introduces a Capacity Fidelity Controller (CFC) that monitors per-pool fidelity and applies a short-window soft-surge fallback to preserve promises without hard preemption. The change is conservative and opt-in via a cluster feature flag; default rollout is canary to 10% of pools.

What this PR does (single-string changelog): Implements the CFC control loop (continuous sample->score->action) with a fidelity score computed as a percentile-corrected ratio of observed throughput to committed throughput over multiple windows; adds a soft-surge fallback path that temporarily relaxes per-tenant concurrency caps and switches to a higher-overcommit pool variant when fidelity drops below thresholds; emits new telemetry (fidelity_score, fidelity_slip, surge_fallback_invocations, pool_variant_switches) and a per-pool "fidelity_profile" exported via the Console and Prometheus; exposes 3 knobs via Dedicated config: fidelity_target_pct (default 95), fidelity_window_secs (default 300), and surge_fallback_budget (default 0.1 of pool capacity).

Files and areas touched (high-level): pkg/autoscaler/capacity_fidelity_controller.go (core loop and action reconciler), pkg/autoscaler/score/windowed_percentile.go (percentile estimator), internal/allocator/pool_variant.go (soft overcommit pool variants and safe-switch logic), telemetry/metrics.yaml (definitions and new Prometheus counters/gauges), console/api/v1/pool_profiles.go (profile API surface), cmd/redwoodctl/feature_flags.go (flag to enable/disable), tests/autoscaler/cfc_integration_test.go (end-to-end warmup and failover path), tests/autoscaler/unit_windowed_percentile_test.go, docs/ops/capacity-fidelity.md (operational runbook).

Behavior and compatibility notes: The controller is opt-in; existing pools are unchanged until their pool annotation is set to accept fidelity enforcement. When enabled, CFC only enforces soft actions (temporary surge budget, pool-variant switch with automatic revert). There are safeguards: a maximum of 3 variant switches per hour per pool, and a backoff that decays over a 15m cooling period. The fidelity score is designed to be robust to short-lived spikes by using a median-of-percentiles estimator. No model or inference contract changes; SDKs unchanged.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Deploy binary with telemetry gated to canary clusters. 3) Enable on 10% of dedicated pools for 48h with verbose logging. 4) If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 2 weeks. Alerts: added fidelity_slip_rate > 0.5 for >10m triggers pager (SRE).

Performance and cost considerations: The controller samples aggregated per-pool counters at 10s resolution and maintains small in-memory percentile sketches (approx 2KB per pool). In our canary, additional CPU overhead was ~0.9% on autoscaler nodes and Prometheus cardinality increased by ~18 custom metrics per pool. Surge fallback can increase short-term GPU utilization but limits by surge_fallback_budget.

Testing and validation: unit tests for estimator and action gating; synthetic integration tests that emulate headroom loss and validate fidelity retention; canary smoke results included in commit history. The PR includes a linear ticket linking the performance validation harness (ENG-5042).

Checklist: [x] design doc link in Linear (ENG-5042) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] telemetry defined [x] Console surface minimal API [x] runbook draft

Related work: complements recent warm-pool and burst-budget work but focuses on fidelity guarantees rather than fairshare. See ENG-4877 (warm-pool heuristics) and ENG-5050 for telemetry alignment.

review_comments: Diego Mendez: Can you clarify how fidelity_score behaves with bursty short workloads? Suggest adding a short-circuit to avoid triggering for <30s windows.
Aisha N. Patel: Added median-of-percentiles estimator and clamped min-window to 60s to avoid noisy short workloads; updated tests to cover 30s/60s scenarios.
Lina Zhou: The pool_variant switch looks racy with concurrent allocator updates; add a leader-guard and CAS on pool resourceVersion.
Samir Gupta: Added leader-guard and CAS; also limited switches to 3/hour per-pool and added exponential backoff state.
Diego Mendez: CI flaked on integration e2e initially, reran and all green. Approving post-rerun.
